displayDescription: A floating porcelain egg opens to show its own sun and cloud, which tether out satellites into a connected system under dusk light.
styleRenderer: three.js r186 (WebGL, MeshPhysicalMaterial, PCF soft shadow maps, fog)
HTML/CSS (stationary dusk sky gradient and Georgia typography)
motionEngine: GSAP paused timeline created inline in index.html and registered at window.__timelines["video"]; scene.js (window.SurrealScene.build) adds all tweens. GSAP is the sole owner of scene state, the camera dolly and text opacity/y.
limitations: Blender was not used, at the user's instruction. The scene is real-time Three.js WebGL, not path-traced: no global illumination, caustics or subsurface scattering. The porcelain is approximated with clearcoat and sheen.
Shadows come from a single PCF soft shadow map; the inner sun's point light casts no shadows.
The sky is a stationary CSS gradient behind a transparent canvas. The camera only translates (its orientation is fixed), so the horizon stays registered at 488px.
Subtitle colour #C9D6DD is a light tint of the slate-blue family. The suggested #617C8B is only about 2.3:1 on the dusk sky, so #617C8B is kept for the cloud and the blue satellites.

BACKGROUND_REVIEW.json has no matched sources or contact sheets, so no source-frame evidence was applied. STYLE.json has no preview_recipes, so the refresh demonstrates only the scene-dependent background.

The bundled three.js contains Math.random (UUID and random-vector helpers) and requestAnimationFrame (unused animation loop). Neither affects rendered pixels; every frame is redrawn from GSAP time on seek.
The title copy uses Georgia, which the renderer resolves automatically. Didot/Bodoni were dropped because no @font-face source exists for them, so the serif is less high-contrast than the reference.
